meta.title: Executive dashboard
meta.seoTitle: Executive dashboard demo: sales, finance and receivables
meta.seoDescription: Interactive demo with sample data from a Colombian company (or your own CSV): sales vs. target, margin, receivables aging, 13-week cash flow, statistical projection, rule-based alerts, guided questions and a PDF report. Everything is calculated in your browser.

shell.sidebarSample: Sample data: the company, customers, tax ID and figures are fictitious and generated in your browser.
shell.sidebarUpload: You are viewing the data from your file. It never leaves your browser; reloading takes you back to the sample data.
shell.sampleHint: Fictitious company and figures, generated with a fixed seed so every view adds up.
shell.uploadHint: Data from the CSV you uploaded. It is processed only in your browser.
shell.currency: Figures in Colombian pesos (COP), excluding VAT

pnl.note: Budgeted cost = sales target × last year’s cost ratio. Budgeted expenses = same period last year + 6%. Sales and cost are the sum of the period’s invoices, the same ones you see in Overview and Customers.

cash.title: 13-week cash flow
cash.subtitle: Projection from the cut-off date ({date}). Hover over each week to see inflows and outflows.
cash.legendMarkers: IVA = bimonthly VAT payment · P = service bonus (prima)
cash.method: How it is calculated: open receivables are collected on their due date plus each customer’s average delay (whatever is already past that delay is spread over the next 4 weeks, and invoices more than 180 days past due, {excluded}, are not projected); projected sales are collected according to each customer’s terms and delay (on average {days} days); suppliers paid at {supplierDays} days; payroll twice a month, service bonus in December, rent on the 5th and other expenses spread across the month.
cash.taxNote: Bimonthly VAT is 19% of taxable sales minus VAT on taxable purchases. The payment date ({date}) is an example: the real one depends on the last digit of the tax ID in the DIAN calendar.

moves.title: Key movements
moves.subtitle: Largest collections, payroll, rent and VAT paid in {period}.
moves.note: Collections include invoiced VAT. They come from the same dashboard invoices (payment date); payroll and rent come from the month’s expenses.

ask.title: Guided questions
ask.subtitle: Pick a question or type it. Answers are calculated with the figures for {period}.

q.customersDown: Which customers buy less than last year?
q.cityGoal: Which city or site is furthest from target?
q.overdue: Who accounts for most past-due receivables?
q.cash8: How much cash will I have in 8 weeks?
q.forecast: How would the next 3 months close?

ask.miss: This demo only answers the guided questions above (margin, customers, targets by city, receivables, cash and projection) and did not recognize “{text}”. In your project, free-form questions are answered by an AI model over authorized views of your data.
ask.note: No AI in this demo: each guided question runs a calculation on the same dashboard data and shows how it was done. What you type is matched against keywords in your browser; it is not sent to any server.

a.margin: In {period} gross margin went from {prev} to {now} ({delta}). The line that dropped the most is {line}.
a.customersDown: {count, plural, one {# customer buys} other {# customers buy}} less than in the same period last year in {period}; together that is {lost} less.
a.customersDownNone: No customer buys less than in the same period last year in {period}.
a.cash8: At the end of week 8 ({date}) you would have {balance}. The lowest point is {min}, in the week of {minDate}.
a.cityGoal: The {dim} furthest from target in {period} is {city}: at {pct} of its target, {gap} below.
a.noData: There is no target to compare against in this period.
a.overdue: Receivables more than 60 days past due total {total} as of {date}. {count, plural, one {One customer accounts} other {# customers account}} for {share}.
a.forecast: At the current pace, {from} – {to} would close at {value}, {pct} of target (80% range: {low} to {high}).
a.forecastNoGoal: At the current pace, {from} – {to} would close at {value} (80% range: {low} to {high}).

how.margin: Margin = (sales − cost) ÷ sales, by line, comparing the period with the same months of {prevYear}. Lines are sorted from the largest drop to the largest increase.
how.customersDown: For each customer I compare the period’s sales with the same months of {prevYear} (only customers who were already buying) and sort by the difference in pesos.
how.cash8: This is week 8 of the 13-week cash flow in Finance: it starts from cash at cut-off ({date}: {start}) and adds projected collections and subtracts payments week by week.
how.cityGoal: Target for each city or site = its sales in the same months of {prevYear} + {goal}%. Attainment = sales ÷ target.
how.overdue: I add up open invoices more than 60 days past due at the end of the period and group them by customer.
how.forecastSeasonal: Each month = sales of the same month last year × growth of the last 3 months vs. the same months last year ({growth}). The 80% band comes from the error this method had in the months already known (deviation {sigma}).
how.forecastTrend: Linear trend of the last months with data. The 80% band comes from the deviation from that trend ({sigma}).
